# Maintained security backports

These four packages are explicit repository-local forks of upstream libraries, not claimed upstream patched releases. Each fork records the registry tarball integrity, retains the original license/attribution, and includes the exact source patch. No install hooks or unpatched minified build is distributed. npm overrides apply the same fork throughout the dependency tree.

* `braces` 3.0.3: GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm. Limit parser nesting and validate ASTs iteratively before recursive compile, expand or stringify. Reject cyclic or excessive caller-supplied ASTs. Cap Cartesian/range expansion at 10,000 outputs even if callers disable the upstream range limit.
* `node-forge` 1.4.0: GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv. Require exactly one algorithm OID and at most one primitive, empty NULL parameter inside RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 DigestAlgorithm. Reject additional nested values before comparing the digest.
  Additional CodeQL findings are fixed with linear PEM boundary/header parsing, native whitespace trimming, dangerous cookie key rejection, and bounded dedicated-worker messages with origin checks. These changes retain certificate and encrypted private-key round trips and are covered by security regressions.
* `sprintf-js` 1.1.3: GHSA-hp3w-g68c-fv3c. Bound width and precision before formatting, including the direct pre-parsed formatting API.

* `deepmerge` 4.3.1: GHSA-gcqx-w48m-w2h4 has no fixed upstream release as of 2026-10-31. All writes into the merged result define own data properties instead of invoking prototype setters. This protects both copied target keys and merged source keys; ordinary nested values, arrays, custom array merging, and enumerable symbols remain covered by regressions. See `deepmerge/UPSTREAM.md` for provenance and `deepmerge/SECURITY.patch` for the full patch.

The `minimatch` directory is a compatibility adapter, not a matcher fork: it delegates to the exact patched upstream minimatch 11.0.3 package, while preserving legacy callable CommonJS and modern named/ESM interfaces. Glob 9+ consumers use patched upstream glob 14.0.3; older callback consumers retain their existing API. Zod uses patched upstream 4.6.7.

The adapter is installed from `medguide-minimatch-compat-1.0.0.tgz` so npm resolves identical package bytes at every dependency depth instead of creating nested local-directory links. Its readable sources remain in `minimatch/`; a regression compares all archived files with those sources. After changing the adapter, regenerate it with `npm pack ./vendor/minimatch --pack-destination ./vendor --ignore-scripts`, update the lockfile, and run the full clean-install and bundle checks.

`npm run test:security` verifies malformed inputs/signatures are rejected while normal glob expansion, formatting and RSA signatures still work. It also checks prototype safety, module compatibility, cancellation without background traversal, and oversized-array validation. Replace these local forks with verified upstream fixed releases as soon as available; the owner must review upstream security changes weekly via the scheduled audit. Library-specific dependency scans remain necessary alongside npm audit because a repository-local fork cannot inherit upstream advisory coverage automatically.
